ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent in ChatGPT designed to execute tasks across applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The release underscores the rapid shift from chatbots toward task-oriented workplace automation.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models for real-time interaction
items.summary: OpenAI also introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The launch points to growing emphasis on low-latency, multimodal assistants.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 to developers
items.summary: Meta debuted Muse Spark 1.1 and opened preview access to developers, positioning the model against Anthropic and OpenAI in the enterprise and API market. Reuters reported the release as a notable expansion of Meta’s AI model strategy.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI introduced Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model to date with a focus on coding and agentic tasks. The launch adds to the fast-moving race among frontier model providers.

items.title: Meta announces major new data center in Alberta
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand compute capacity for AI. The move reflects the industry-wide push to secure more infrastructure for training and deployment.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights continued attention to AI governance and mission oversight.

items.title: New York Times-led group seeks sanctions against OpenAI in copyright case
items.summary: A coalition of newspapers asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about its ability to search systems for evidence related to copyright claims. The dispute is another sign that AI training-data litigation remains a major industry risk.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for violations of data protection rules. Regulators continue to scrutinize consumer AI products over privacy and compliance issues.

items.title: Ollama raises $65 million Series B
items.summary: Ollama, a developer tool for running open-weight AI models locally, raised a $65 million Series B led by Theory Ventures. The funding reflects strong investor interest in local and open-model infrastructure.

items.title: Cognition releases SWE-1.7 for fast coding workflows
items.summary: Cognition released SWE-1.7, a model trained from Kimi K2.7 and available in Devin at 1,000 tokens per second. The company says it approaches frontier-level capability at lower cost, reinforcing the race to make coding agents faster and cheaper.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation games will go digital-only after January 2028
items.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment has confirmed that production of physical PS5 game discs for new titles will end in January 2028, marking a major shift toward digital distribution on PlayStation. The announcement has also sparked broader discussion about the future of physical media in gaming.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass reportedly fell short of Microsoft’s growth targets
items.summary: Reports indicate Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Game Pass did not grow as Microsoft had expected, with subscriber numbers said to be tens of millions below prior targets. The news adds to ongoing scrutiny of Microsoft’s gaming strategy.

items.title: Bethesda confirms Oblivion Remastered is coming to Switch 2
items.summary: Bethesda Softworks has confirmed that The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on 11 August 2026. The announcement is one of the most notable platform-release updates in recent gaming news.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games has settled its legal dispute with former contractor Hayden Cohen, who was accused of leaking confidential Fortnite collaboration details. Epic also dropped its monetary claims as part of the settlement.

items.title: Square Enix says future Final Fantasy remakes will take distinct directions
items.summary: Square Enix said at its June 24 shareholder meeting that future Final Fantasy remakes will each be developed with a different approach depending on the title and market conditions. The statement suggests a more flexible remake strategy for the franchise going forward.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly increases investment in MachineGames
items.summary: Insider reporting says Microsoft is significantly increasing its investment in MachineGames after the commercial success of Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and the continued popularity of Wolfenstein. If accurate, the move signals continued confidence in the studio’s future projects.

items.title: Subnautica 2 reportedly surpasses 5 million copies sold
items.summary: WN Hub reports that Subnautica 2 has sold more than 5 million copies. If confirmed by the publisher, it would be one of the standout commercial milestones in recent game sales news.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 sales surpass one million copies
items.summary: WN Hub reports that Frostpunk 2 has now sold more than 1 million copies. The milestone reflects continued strong demand for the city-building survival sequel.

items.title: Nintendo to discontinue original Switch models in Europe
items.summary: Nintendo has announced that sales of the original Switch, Switch Lite, and OLED models will stop in Europe next year because of changes tied to EU battery legislation. The decision marks a significant hardware-transition development ahead of the next console cycle.

items.title: Obsidian reportedly cancels Avowed sequel amid Xbox restructuring
items.summary: Gadgets 360 reports that Obsidian has cancelled a planned Avowed sequel and shifted work toward a new Fallout project as part of Xbox restructuring. The report also ties the move to broader cuts and studio changes inside Microsoft gaming.
